newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen 50 cts lower, Brent up 10 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen 50 cts lower, Brent up 10 cts.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were expected to open lower on Monday, tracking a fall in the crude price from late Friday, while Brent was seen opening slightly higher on overnight gains in Singapore.

July gas oil was expected to open 50 to 75 cents lower from its previous closing price of $162.75 a tonne. August Brent was seen opening around 10 cents higher from its Friday close of $17.76 a barrel.
With few factors to feed to, however, dealers saw both markets drifting.
"We're bereft of any news, really. We're going to be looking for direction," one dealer said.
The market was still awaiting developments in the ongoing Iraq/U.N. oil-for-food saga, with question marks hanging over Iraq's commitment to usher the deal through.
Baghdad's U.N. envoy Nizar Hamdoon said on Friday Iraq had no interest in delaying its oil sales, but wanted assurances on U.N. plans to distribute food and medicine bought with the proceeds.
Dealers saw Brent very much rangebound until there were further developments. Resistance was cited at $18.15 a barrel, and support at $17.61 to $17.71 .
